Triage: lands in `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectPivotTable.tsx` ⇒ **`domain:ui`**; **type `Bug`, `priority:p2`, `pm:queue`.**

**Class (a), and the strongest possible evidence for a fix shape: the identical statement was removed one block over, and that removal has landed.**

```ts
const merged = { ...(schema.filter || {}), ...baseFilter };   // ObjectPivotTable.tsx:269
```

⇒ Spreading an **array** yields index keys, so an authored `[['region','=','emea']]` becomes `{ '0': [...] }` — a key the query layer ignores. ⭐ **Nothing errors**: the drawer opens, looks right, and is scoped by the clicked cell alone. The widget's own narrowing is silently gone.

**Measured 2026-09-10T19:26:48Z:** objectui**#8944** is `closed` and **PR #9016 merged 19:09:29Z** — seventeen minutes before this card reached triage. ⇒ The corrected composition is **on `main` now**. Port it; ⛔ do not re-derive it, and ⛔ do not invent a second shape for the same defect.

## ⭐ Why p2 and not p3 — the direction matters

The widget's filter is what **NARROWS**. Dropping it silently means the drawer shows **more** than the author scoped, not less. ⚠️ A user reading a drill-down cannot tell the difference between "these are the rows behind this cell" and "these are the rows behind this cell plus everything the widget filter was meant to exclude".

⛔ Not p1: the server still enforces its own access rules, so this is wrong *scoping*, ⛔ not an authorization bypass. Nothing a user cannot already see is exposed.

⭐ **The filer re-derived every reading itself** on `origin/main` `bbf068db1` with controls, and flagged where it contradicts PR #9016's acceptance note rather than deferring to it. ⇒ Dispatch on this card's readings; where the two disagree, the card says which and why.

⚠️ `yes` because the card's second finding may pull a **declaration** into the fix: `filter?: any` is grown on a **local props intersection**, and declaring it on `PivotTableSchema` instead would widen a published authorable surface. ⛔ It may also turn out that routing through `composeDrillFilter` needs no declaration at all — but the rule is 「拿不准 ⇒ 按 `yes`」 and a `no` cannot be revised on delivery. Hang the carriers on both sides with the draft PR and report the `--pair` exit code (`PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui`, exit by **redirect**, ⛔ never after a pipe).

## Preconditions verified before dispatch, each with a lit control

```
composeDrillFilter   packages/core/src/utils/drill-down.ts:247   EXPORTED        (the seam exists)
the defect           ObjectPivotTable.tsx:269                    LIVE
  control            baseFilter, same file                       2 hits
the reference        ObjectChart.tsx uses composeDrillFilter      3 hits
```

⇒ seam present, defect present, and a landed reference implementation to read. ⚠️ Line numbers are from **09:1xZ** and `main` is moving fast — re-derive them.

## ZONE 1 — what to build

`ObjectPivotTable.tsx:269` composes its drill filter by spreading:

```ts
const merged = { ...(schema.filter || {}), ...baseFilter };
```

Spreading an **array** yields index keys, so an authored `[['region','=','emea']]` becomes `{ '0': [...] }` — a key the query layer ignores. ⚠️ **Direction matters:** the widget's filter is what **narrows**, so losing it makes the drilled list a **superset** — rows the pivot itself was scoped to exclude. Silent, and the worse direction.

⭐ **The fix is probably not a second local repair.** `composeDrillFilter` already names and applies the rule (`widget.filter ∧ drill.filter`, via `mergeFilterNodes`), and routing this site through it is the shape objectui#8944's ruling preferred. ⚠️ **But confirm the pivot's two drill sinks take the same dialect before assuming the seam drops in** — the card says so and it is the kind of assumption that costs a round.

## ⚠️ Why the previous "unreachable" judgement does not hold — do not re-derive it wrong

PR objectui#9016's notes record this file as *"not the same defect — `PivotTableSchema.filter` declares no array arm, so it is unreachable."* The observation is true; the inference is not, and the card measured why:

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| `PivotTableSchema` members named `filter` | **0** (control: 12 other members counted by the same probe) |
| `BaseSchema` members named `filter` | **0** (control: 21 others) |
| declarations of `filter` reaching the component | **1** — a local props intersection, `filter?: any` |

⇒ `PivotTableSchema.filter` declares no array arm because **it declares no `filter` at all**. The type that admits the value is `any` — *strictly more permissive* than the chart's union, not less. ⛔ Nothing in the type system stops an author writing the array form here.

## ZONE 2 — the third site, and an honest limit on my own check

The card says: ⚠️ *"`ObjectMetricWidget` was routed through the shared `DrillDownDrawer` by PR objectui#8999 — check whether it composes its own filter too, rather than assuming this is the last copy."*

I probed it and found **neither** `composeDrillFilter` nor the spread-merge spelling. ⛔ **That is not an all-clear, and I am not giving you one:** I checked **one spelling**, and "this pattern is absent" is not "it does not compose its own filter." ⇒ **you check it properly**, and report what you find either way. A zero from my probe is exactly the kind of reading this lane has been burned by five times today.

## ZONE 3 — fences

- ⛔ Not an `ObjectChart` change — objectui#8944, landed as PR objectui#9016. It is your **reference**, not your subject.
- ⛔ Do not fix `ObjectMetricWidget` in this PR even if it is a third copy. Report it; a third site is its own card or an explicit widening you ask for first.
- ⚠️ The second finding (`filter?: any` grown on a props intersection — the objectui#6357 second-declaration class) is **adjacent and may be the better fix**. The card notes the comment directly beneath it records that the data-scope binding key *used to be* declared that way and was removed for exactly that reason — ⇒ that cleanup **stopped one member short**. ⭐ Decide the two together and say why; ⛔ do not silently do only the composition and leave `any` in place without naming the choice.

## ZONE 4 — stop conditions, each as the harm it guards

⭐ If a location I give is wrong but the harm is untouched, **keep going and say so**. PM claims are in scope for falsification and a clean stop on a falsified PM premise is a **full success** — this seat's dispatch has been falsified **nine** times today, including an acceptance rule that would have passed against the broken tree on two of three keys, and every correction improved the result.

- **Stop if routing through `composeDrillFilter` changes the drilled row set for the object-form filter** (the shape the in-repo corpus actually authors). The harm is fixing an unreachable array arm while regressing the reachable object one.
- **Stop if declaring `filter` on `PivotTableSchema` would narrow what an author can write today.** `any` accepts everything; a declared union may not. The harm is a silent refusal of existing authored metadata — ⛔ measure before you narrow.

## ZONE 5 — acceptance

- ⭐ **The oracle is the composed filter's row set**, ⛔ not the composed object's shape. The card is explicit: every type- and doc-level gate reads this site **green** today, and *"a green that cannot go red on this defect is not evidence."* PR objectui#9016's new pin uses the row-set shape and can be reused.
- The array form: an authored `[['region','=','emea']]` plus a clicked cell → the drilled rows are the **intersection**, ⛔ not the superset.
- The object form: unchanged (regression guard, and the shape the corpus authors).
- Ablate the routing and show the array case reds; restore and prove the tree clean **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty + blob hash back to HEAD's), ⛔ never by an exit code.
